interpretation: The 32-iteration run diverges from the 64-iteration reference at the first sampled accepted state (step 8) and has many numeric differences despite identical row keys and source assets. This is a changed-physics sensitivity, not a repeatability result.

Late window COM displacement and root-frame decomposition show whether differences are mostly carrier translation, root rotation orbit, or relative articulation; they do not identify the force or constraint cause.

Impulse-weighted pre-step tangential Jv and sampled skin selector changes are observations on their recorded bases. They are not post-solve slip measurements or proof that iteration count caused baseline drift.

No iteration count is recommended or adopted from this comparison. A faster run is not sufficient; the 32 arm must be judged on complete accepted trajectory, anatomy, contact quality, and the user-facing behavior.

observer_integrity.scope: both observer streams verified; 32/64 physical CSV values are expected to differ

scope: One 310 s native observer-on run changed stand contact iterations from 64 to 32. Assets, runtime, physiology arguments, timestep/horizon, and observer settings match; only output paths and this iteration value differ. It is not a qualification or a causal proof for drift.
